subject: Discovery recap: inference pricing targets & $/1M benchmarking
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@curepath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference pricing targets & $/1M benchmarking

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap + asks so we have alignment and can move to a pricing workshop next week.

Call highlights (my notes):
- Primary product: document ingestion + summarization + Q&A for clinical docs.
- Expected inference traffic: 30M tokens/mo initially, growing to ~150–200M tokens/mo in 9–12 months (peak windows during batch processing).
- Latency SLOs: p95 generation < 600ms for short responses, support for larger summarization runs (2–4s acceptable).
- Data posture: must be private (VPC preferred), SOC2 compliance required, keys in customer KMS.
- Main procurement constraints: fixed monthly budget envelope and preference for predictable $/1M token unit.

What you asked us to confirm: target $/1M token range and comparative context vs other hosts (OpenAI/Anthropic and a couple of open-model hosts). I captured the ranges you gave on the call: $35–60 per 1M tokens for the first 30M tier, trending down to $8–18/1M at 150M+ depending on model mix. Please confirm if those ranges reflect your expectations.

Next asks from our side (quick):
1) Can you upload the usage breakouts (token mix across short chat vs long summarization, and monthly ramp) — I left my email for a spreadsheet in the call.
2) Does CurePath have a preferred list of models (OpenAI, Anthropic, local Llama variants, etc.) or are you open to a recommended mix from us to meet cost targets?
3) Are there procurement constraints we should mirror in a formal quote (term length, invoice cadence, PO process)?

I'll loop in Ben and Karthik to put together a baseline $/1M comparison grid (OpenAI/Anthropic/open-hosts + Redwood hosted/dedicated/private options) and propose a 60-minute pricing workshop.

Proposed workshop times (PT): Thu 5/6 10:00–11:00, Thu 5/6 15:00–16:00, or Mon 5/10 09:00–10:00. Which works best?

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference pricing targets & $/1M benchmarking

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the concise recap. Confirming the high-level numbers from our side:
- Baseline month 1: 25–35M tokens (mix: ~70% short interaction tokens (QA/chat), 30% long-run summarization and batch jobs).
- Ramp plan: 3x by month 6, 6x by month 12 (estimates in attached spreadsheet).
- Top-level budget target: we are trying to get total inference costs under $7–9k/mo in month 1 (we know that's aggressive) and a target blended $/1M of $20–30 initially — with a stretch goal toward $10–18/1M once volumes mature.

Notes:
- We are open to model mixing to hit the blended target. OpenAI for highest-quality chat, Anthropic for safety-sensitive flows, and cheap open-host variants for bulk summarization is a reasonable approach.
- Procurement: 60-day PO + net30 invoicing likely. Multi-year committed pricing would be considered but needs exec sign-off.

Attached the spreadsheet with token breakdowns and a conservative ramp. Let us know if you want any clarifications.

Cheers,
Alex
VP Product, CurePath
alex.morgan@curepath.com | +1 646-555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>

Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference pricing targets & $/1M benchmarking

Alex / team — quick market synthesis + baseline benchmarking for workshop. High-level assumptions visible in the attached grid (pdf): model mix scenarios, gross token rates, and Redwood list vs host comps.

Summary bullets:
- Market comps (public list/observed):
  • OpenAI (gpt-4.1-like): observed effective $/1M for chat-quality flows ~ $55–75/1M (varies with context length and streaming).
  • Anthropic (Claude-Next-like): ~ $45–65/1M for higher-safety/chat flows on comparable contexts.
  • Open-model hosts (various providers): bulk discount paths down to $8–25/1M depending on quantization and model parity for batch tasks.
- Redwood positioning: our hosted API list will sit near the high end of open-host bulk rates for very low-latency, higher-quality endpoints but offers better SLO, fallbacks, and no-ops for customers. Dedicated pools materially reduce per-token unit cost for sustained volumes (we model a 2.5–4x reduction in variable cost depending on batchability and KV cache reuse). Private on-prem (customer-managed infra) can drop unit cost further but shifts ops to CurePath.

Concrete target rows I recommend for the quote (blended by token type):
- Conservative (mix: 70% chat, 30% summarization): target blended $/1M = $28–36 (month 1) -> $12–20 (mature volumes)
- Aggressive (mix: 40% chat, 60% batch summarization on quantized models): target blended $/1M = $18–24 (month 1) -> $8–14 (mature volumes)

Risks / notes:
- Short-chat heavy workloads are harder to batch; we'll need to size dedicated capacity if CurePath expects low-p95 latency and high chat volume.
- Quantization for summarization runs reduces cost but can impact output quality; suggest an eval run on their 5K sample corpus before committing to the lowest-cost profile.

I attached a simple pricing-grid with per-model effective $/1M lines (OpenAI/Anthropic/open-host observed rates) and Redwood configuration rows (hosted, dedicated small pool, dedicated reserved, private). We'll walk through the assumptions in the workshop and produce an initial committed offer to match CurePath's target band.

Proposed next step: 60-min pricing workshop where we review the attached grid, pick a model-mix profile, and align on committed volume + term. I can cover the dedicated sizing and cost math.

Ben
Director, Growth Pricing | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0174

1) Pricing workshop (60 min) — Ben-led. Please confirm Thu 5/13 10:00 PT or Mon 5/10 09:00 PT.
2) Evaluation plan: we run a 2-week quality-vs-cost batch evaluation on your 5K sample corpus (Redwood supplies a quantized instance + tooling; CurePath provides sample data). This will validate blended $/1M outcomes for the summarization-heavy slices.
3) Draft commercial: Based on workshop, we'll send a starter committed offer (3 month ramp commit + 12 month term optional) with tiered unit rates and a dedicated pool sizing appendix.

Finance note (cc): we typically present 3 price bands in the initial commercial: list (hosted) / reserved (dedicated small pool) / private (customer infra) so procurement can see tradeoffs.

Please reply with which workshop slot works and whether your procurement team wants us to draft the PO path in parallel. Happy to answer any clarifying questions.
